title: Training Note — The Courtesy Allowance on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Training Note — The Courtesy Allowance on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

*Basis questions answered for the finance desk. The number of courtesy give-backs allowed in a rolling twelve months and the minimum courtesy tenure are the figures the fee schedule states for the plan's promotional term.*

**What may be given back as a courtesy?** A late fee already charged on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan may be given back as a courtesy a limited number of times in a rolling twelve months, the allowance being set by the term.

**May the same charge be given back twice?** No. A courtesy give-back is granted against a late fee only when no give-back already stands against that same late fee entry, and a give-back is never granted against a charge that has already been given back. The billing history is the evidence: a give-back entry referring to that late fee entry as its source means one already stands.

**How long must the plan have been billing?** A courtesy give-back is granted only when the plan has been billing for at least the minimum courtesy tenure in whole calendar months counted from the date the plan began billing. Courtesy tenure is counted in whole calendar months from the date the plan began billing, and where the anniversary day does not exist in the closing month the boundary falls on the last day of that month. A plan that has been billing exactly the minimum number of whole months satisfies the condition.

**Do other give-backs use up the allowance?** The clause that read "A give-back made because the bank confirmed its own error, or made to put right a service failure of the chain's own, is recorded under its own reason and does not consume the courtesy allowance." is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis for a give-back made to put right a failure of the chain's own handling.

**What happens when the allowance is exhausted?** Where the allowance is exhausted the desk does not give the fee back and the request is answered by explaining the allowance.

## Tenure at the boundary (hypothetical dates)

A plan began billing on 20 May on a term whose minimum courtesy tenure is 6 whole calendar months. The boundary falls on 20 November.

| Handling date | Tenure condition |
|---|---|
| 19 November | Not met: fewer than 6 whole calendar months have passed |
| 20 November | Met: at least 6 whole calendar months have passed, and the boundary day itself satisfies it |
| 21 November | Met |

superseded_clauses: A give-back made because the bank confirmed its own error, or made to put right a service failure of the chain's own, is recorded under its own reason and does not consume the courtesy allowance.
